DEC-239. First Track A session in six that ends in shipped code rather than a document. Closed the two funnel leaks DAL-218 measured: the homepage (225 visitors/mo, the site's top page) had no Treesmith CTA at all because the promo block was wired into six builders but never build-dashboard.py; /treesmith.html asked for the install with plain text buttons, now the vendors' official badge artwork. Named the real blocker as DAL-242: DEC-237's two highest-leverage levers, ratings (DAL-230) and paywall reachability (DAL-224), both need Benedict and both have sat in Backlog.

DEC-240. DAL-173 turned from a four-month-old email draft into a standing mechanism, per Benedict's overnight spec: send_treesmith_intro.py mails the Treesmith intro to each NEW treestock subscriber 7 days after signup, once and never again. Proof-of-concept sent to Benedict; nightly cron installed but a logged no-op until he creates the approval flag. Existing 13 subscribers excluded by a start-date gate so flipping the switch cannot pre-empt the separate broadcast he wants to approve (DAL-221). DAL-173 handed to Benedict awaiting approval. Also found while writing the email: replies to every treestock email we have ever sent bounce, because the sending subdomain mail.treestock.com.au has no MX or A record and no sender sets a Reply-To, while the welcome and intro emails both invite replies (DAL-243, Q46). Proposed DAL-244 to instrument the subscribe funnel, since subscribers are now the input to an automated Treesmith drip rather than a vanity count.

DEC-246 / DAL-115: rebuilt the community data post on 142 days x 27 nurseries. The April draft was stale (White Sapote, its headline 'rarest', is now in stock somewhere every day) and had broken price ranges. National rarity has largely resolved: 92 of 108 species in stock somewhere on all 142 days. The real finding is state reachability, with 73 of 108 species never once buyable in TAS, and WA far less cut off than assumed. Handed to Benedict to post. Proposed DAL-254 (citable reachability page, the linkable asset DEC-245 said we lacked) and DAL-255 (SA nurseries).

DEC-247 / DAL-177: measured 36 AU App Store terms and found the ASO plan was aimed at the wrong field. Our subtitle contains 'garden journal' verbatim and we are not in the top 191, while the top 4 are 0-to-6 rating apps carrying the phrase in their NAME. Recommended renaming to 'TreeSmith: Fruit Tree Tracker' (we are already #7 there, Grove took #1 on name alone at 0 ratings) rather than retargeting the subtitle and keyword field. Also found both live store descriptions state Pro includes cloud backup, which is false and is the one thing that must be fixed regardless. Handed to Benedict. Proposed DAL-256 (App Store Connect funnel: discovery vs listing) and DAL-257 (4-week rank re-measure with a falsifiable prediction).

DEC-248: the referral ceiling published this morning was exactly 10.0x too small (1,245 clicks x 3% x $70 x 8% = $209/mo, published as $21). Full-coverage referral clears $100/mo at today's traffic above ~1.2% conversion, and the top 3 nurseries alone cover the A$8.20/mo cash burn ~4x. Also separated the two targets (A$8.20 infra vs ~A$162 full self-funding) and separated paid placement (declined twice) from performance referral (never asked). Plan to the first dollar: join Primal Fruits' free self-serve program for the conversion MEASUREMENT (~$2/mo revenue, prices all 1,245 clicks), then ask the top 3. Kill condition recorded. Second half of the session reduced Benedict's queue from 8 items to a ranked 3, recommending DAL-165 close and DAL-173 cancel.

DEC-249. Posted to DAL-249 and DAL-250; recommended DAL-228 be deferred. Nothing added to Benedict's queue.

DEC-250. Shipped DAL-215: regenerated archive_links.json from a fresh clone of rfcarchives.org.au (30 -> 41 species, 216 links, clean superset, zero existing entries changed), plus three generator fixes (placeholder 'Title' titles dropped, mostly-uppercase titles de-shouted, a dead ALIAS kiwifruit->kiwi removed). 1950 tests pass, goldens unaffected. Real figures: 521 sends not 81, 48 clicks not 8, 43.2% open rate, and all 13 subscribers engaged rather than 2 'never emailed' (those two are our best converters). Third pagination truncation in three days after gsc_analysis.py and Plausible. DAL-231 answered: yes to one bare-root email a year, but gate it on Q46 because replies currently bounce, and it is worth ~A$1 at 13 subscribers.

DEC-251. Emergency fix, not a ticket from Todo. Two of 13 subscribers had been dropped from every daily digest by an empty plant_categories list: lissandross since 07-21, muffinmotzy since signup on 07-12 (never received one). Also found deploy.sh never restarts subscribe-server (DAL-263), and recommended DAL-192 for cancellation on DEC-249's measured 0.17 outbound clicks per variety page built vs 2.85 for a state page.

DEC-259. Benedict reported the weekly Treesmith digest did not match what he could see in his own app. Both complaints were real. (1) plant_added fires from exactly one screen (plant_form_screen.dart:596), so import and backup restore create plants silently: 291 plants actually held vs 165 add events ever, 43% invisible; his own record is 113 events against a plant count of 160. Ground truth (plant_count_after) was in the payload and had never been read. (2) Every people-count used distinct_id, not person_id: 348 ids vs 297 people, one person carrying 27 ids, installs inflated 17% and phantom ids crushing retention, which is how a returning buyer disappears from the active count in the week they paid. Both fixed, deployed, verified; 2,024 tests up from 2,016. App-side import event proposed, not committed (Benedict's repo). Consolidated as asked: DAL-265 is now the single reporting-accuracy ticket; DAL-269/271/264/267 cancelled into it, backlog 39/40 -> 35/40. Lesson: a human caught this and 16 sessions of automated auditing did not, because no check asked whether the number was one he would recognise.

Also renumbered the duplicate DEC-308 that DEC-311 had recorded as pre-existing; suite green at 3,351. Backlog over cap, so no tickets proposed.

DEC-323. Two measurement guards. DAL-259: test asserting every sitemap-listed static page carries the Plausible tag, and that any other hand-written static page is declared token-bearing or non-public with a reason, so a new untracked page cannot arrive by default; matched on the script src not the bare hostname, because the preconnect/dns-prefetch hints also carry it. Checked failing-then-passing both directions. DAL-262: silent-subscriber alarm, but NOT on the card's rule. '14 days' false-fires on three healthy subscribers who have a 20-day calendar gap in April, when the digest was not running; gaps are now counted in opportunities (sends that reached somebody) with total silence reported separately as a sender outage. Thresholds 3 daily / 2 weekly sit one clear of the measured noise floor (2 and 1). Replayed over all 169 days: 22 subscriber-alert days, 21 of them the real DAL-260 defect, caught 14 days earlier than Benedict found it. Wired into run-all-scrapers.sh, deployed, verified from /opt/dale/scrapers. DAL-248 not started: its own sequencing rule is blocked on an unsent Daleys reply sitting with Benedict.

DEC-324. Deliberately worked a different category: treestock:data_quality had been worked in 3 of the last 5 session-days with no metric movement. Published /fruit-tree-shipping-by-state.html plus /shipping-reachability.json under CC BY 4.0, rebuilt nightly, the first asset treestock owns that is worth citing (DEC-245 concluded we were pricing rented links precisely because we owned nothing linkable on merit). 168 measured days, 119 species, every tracked nursery, joined to published shipping policy. Two caveats carried on the ticket did NOT survive being recomputed: (1) six days in June/July recorded exactly ONE nursery because the scrapers failed, and averaging those outages in understated everything, moving 'in stock somewhere every measured day' from 69 species to 100 of 119; excluded dates are printed in the published JSON. (2) 'the panel grew from 19 to 27' was wrong, day one had 8, so the page now derives the panel from the data every night and shows a recent-30-day average beside the whole-window one. Headline finding: national rarity is largely a myth, state reachability is the real constraint, and 74 of 119 species were never once buyable in Tasmania while WA reached 117. Ten tests pin both arithmetic decisions (nursery-day rollup, outage exclusion) at the OBSERVED values rather than the constant. Suite green at 3,530. Judge on referring domains, which we still cannot see.

DEC-325 + DEC-326. Switched off treestock per the stale-approach gate (data_quality worked 3 of 5 session-days). DAL-241: the scheduled 4-week re-measure of the treestock->Treesmith funnel came due today and the funnel FAILED the exit test it wrote for itself. 30d: 2,044 outbound clicks sitewide, 9 visitors to /treesmith.html, ZERO to either app store; 6mo: 3,132 clicks, 1 ever to the App Store. Traffic grew 64% over the window while store clicks went 1 -> 0. Verified the tags were live, the page instrumented and the badges real hrefs before calling it a zero (DEC-249). Second and more transferable finding: DEC-239's utm_content tagging COULD NEVER have produced the per-surface split, because visit:utm_content is a session-ENTRY dimension and Plausible does not update acquisition attributes on an internal navigation. 1 of 9 visitors carried a tag and that one had entered on /treesmith.html from outside. A tag only works on something that starts a session. Entry-page substitute puts homepage and category landing, the two surfaces DAL-219 added, at zero. CLAUDE.md still called this the 'New primary monetisation path' three sessions after DEC-241 demoted it; corrected with the numbers. DAL-278: shipped store_listing_check.py, which asserts the live copy on all four storefronts against entitlement_provider.dart rather than against a text snapshot, wired into the Monday Treesmith digest. All four storefronts are CORRECT today, including Play which was the unverified one, so this is a guard not a repair. Because an all-green alarm is the easiest kind to get wrong (DEC-265), every rule was proven to fail on text really served by a store: the DEC-262 '50 free plants' sentence, the DEC-247 'Pro: ... cloud backup' sentence, and deletions, which fail rather than pass. Corrected the stale CLAUDE.md warning that both listings are still wrong, which would have had the next session re-fixing a correct listing. 16 new tests, suite 3,546 OK.

Organic 6 -> 4 clicks on 111 -> 286 impressions, still ~entirely branded. Deliberately did NOT open a title-rewrite ticket off the n=1 observation that the one indexed page has a query-shaped title; logged as a hypothesis. DAL-239 shipped today on that same lever, so all of this is its pre-change baseline.

DEC-330. Emergency exception, not a queued ticket. The session prompt's own snapshot line ('Heritage Fruit Trees: 378 products (0 in stock)') read like seasonality and was not. Heritage shut for 2026 on 08-24 and 503ed for two nights, which the dormancy guard shipped that same day handled. From 08-26 it answered HTTP 200 again with the whole catalogue OutOfStock and unpriced (378/0/1), so ok=true reset consecutive_failures to 0 and we were crawling a closed store ~20 min a night, indefinitely, at a nursery Benedict has a relationship with. Runs got LONGER not shorter because a 503 fails fast and a 200 does not. Fixed by judging a run on what it yielded (is_unproductive) rather than on whether the transport stayed quiet. Checked the far end first and it is NOT a data defect: the live page really serves 200 with schema.org/OutOfStock and no price, so the zero is true and untrusted_nurseries() was deliberately untouched. Base rate measured before shipping: 2 occurrences in 27 nurseries x 200 days, both Heritage this week. Streak is 4 of 5 today, so the threshold was not bent to fire on the case in front of me. Also found the priced_collapse alarm shipped 08-24 for this exact failure could not see it (compares to yesterday; yesterday was a failure with no priced field) and posted that to DAL-292. Deliberately did NOT work treestock:data_quality per the stale-approach prompt.
